text:
Brett Pesce has 8 points in 17 games, already more than he managed in 37 games last season. The points aren't why New Jersey plays him 21 minutes a night, but they're a nice sign that he's healthy and comfortable.

The Devils are 12-5 and take 61% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Pesce on the ice at five on five, more than four points better than without him. That's top-tier for a defenseman whose own offense is close to zero: 0.67 individual expected goals all season. His points rate of 1.34 per 60 minutes is well above what we'd expect (0.7 to 1.2), so some cooling is coming.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, from a small nine-game sample, catches both sides of his game. He stops 22% of the entries aimed at him, double the typical rate. But only 20% of his exits keep possession, so he clears it off the glass a lot. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, which feels harsh for a player the Devils lean on this much. We project about 29 points. Mostly, though, watch who isn't scoring when he's out there.
headline: Pesce, the quiet half of a good pair
